Please escalate — our CS and product leads are being copied. We need an ETA on a mitigation and whether you can route our traffic to a stable cohort while you investigate.

From: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 10 Jul 2028 09:32:47 -0400
Subject: Re: Fwd: Re: Increasing 5xxs and massive p99 on auth API (urgent)

Ben / team — quick summary from infra side after initial triage:
- Symptoms: p95 stable around 220–350ms; p99 for first-token and first-byte jumps during pool spin from ~400ms to 8–12s. Increased 5xxs correlate with client timeouts (they abort at ~10s).
- Cause hypothesis: the autoscaler is bringing up cold GPU instances that hit a cold compilation path (kernel JIT) and a lazy filesystem load for quantized weights. On some instances we also see slow NVMe reads on boot that push initialization past the client's timeout.
- Short-term mitigations we can apply immediately (5–15 min):
  * Route SkyPay traffic to an already-warmed dedicated pool (we can map their route to dedicated for the next 12 hours).
  * Increase the pre-warmed standby count for hosted GPU pools for the next 24–48 hours.
  * Turn on a faster boot image variant that skips the JIT path (note: slight token-cost increase).

I'll attach p99 traces and the boot logs. I am also spinning up a small canary group to reproduce.

Attachments: p95_p99_traces_20280710.log

— Marcus
Senior Infrastructure Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Jane Dow <jane.dow@skypay.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Jul 2028 10:06:15 -0400
Subject: Re: Fwd: Re: Increasing 5xxs and massive p99 on auth API (urgent)

Quick technical note from the runtime side:
- I reproduced the long tail locally when the node goes through our new kernel selection logic + quantized weight lazy-load. The cold path hits two things: kernel compilation stalls (~2–6s) and then weight mmap + decompress (~4–7s) on some NVMe nodes. Cumulative delay matches the customer p99s.
- Short term: roll back kernel selector to previous stable commit (pre-20280705) for hostedapi; that removes the JIT stage and reduces cold-init from ~9s to ~1.2s in our tests.
- Medium term: we should implement a small pre-warm handshake (keep KV cache warm + materialize top-k kernels) for high-volume routes and a per-account warm quota.

I'm preparing a patch (proposed_hotfix.diff) and will queue a canary rollback to the warm zone now. Marcus — if you enable dedicated routing for SkyPay, I'll ensure no compatibility gaps.

— Aditya
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference

- Routing: We will move SkyPay to a warmed dedicated pool for the next 24 hours (effectively eliminates cold-start path).
- Hotfix: The runtime team is queuing a rollback of the kernel selector and will canary in the warm zone.
- Credits: We will apply a one-time service credit for the affected window; Ben will follow up with details.

We will keep you updated every hour for the next 6 hours and provide a postmortem within 48 hours. Apologies for the disruption — we know this impacts checkout flow.

Regards,
Evelyn Hart

Date: Tue, 11 Jul 2028 15:45:12 -0400
Subject: Exec note: SkyPay outage window due to autoscale cold-init (summary & approvals)

Leadership —

Summary:
- Customer: SkyPay (large merchant account).
- Impact: elevated 5xxs (~12%) and p99 first-byte latency of 8–12s during autoscaler pool spin events on 2028-07-10 08:50–10:20 ET. Root cause appears to be a combined kernel selector JIT + lazy quantized-weight load on cold nodes plus occasional slow NVMe reads.
- Action taken: routed SkyPay to warmed dedicated pool (mitigation active), runtime rollback queued and canarying in warm zone, increased pre-warm standby counts, customer credited for affected window. Attachments include traces and proposed_hotfix.diff.

Asks / Approvals:
1) Approve immediate application of service credit for SkyPay: proposed credit = 30% of July usage (estimated impact window).
2) Approve rollback in hostedapi prod (we will canary and monitor; rollback reduces cold-init but slightly increases token-cost by using the legacy image path).

If approved, CS will issue the credit and I will coordinate a short customer briefing with the SkyPay CPO. If you want more detail, see INF-8421 and attached logs.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
